messages:
carmen: FYI staging canary for rc-2026-03-21 hit an SBOM provenance flag during deploy, deploy-bot quarantined. Need quick direction on whether to apply a temporary commit-hash pin or allow a controlled rollforward with monitoring.

deploy-bot: [automated] Canary deployment rc-2026-03-21 -> staging
Status: QUARANTINED
Reason: SBOM provenance mismatch: base-image digest not found in signed index
Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/54821

josh: logs?

carmen: pasted the relevant bits below:
```
SBOM check: base-image sha256:abc123... not present in cosign index
vuln-scan: 1 MEDIUM - CVE-2024-9991 in libcrypto (transitive)
policy: provenance_required=true
```

qa-lead: QA ran smoke; the change in question is the baseimage bump from ubuntu20->ubuntu22, no code changes. No regression in functional tests so far.

maria: Legal: is the cosign signature missing or just delayed? If it's a signing issue we might be able to accept a timeboxed exception with evidence.

deploy-bot: Possible actions: `pin-digest`, `rollback-to-previous`, `allow-canary-with-exception`, `delayed-release`. Use `/deploybot action <choice> --approve-by=<user>`

josh: I can repro signature lookup delay — the cosign mirror had a short outage. I can re-run the upload, but it will take ~20m. Alternative is to pin the base-image digest to the new image we built and proceed with canary behind feature-flag.

carmen: Two concerns: 1) vuln CVE-2024-9991 is MEDIUM and present in the new base; 2) change window closes in 90 minutes. If we wait for 20m to re-sign and evidence shows signature volume OK, we can continue normal flow.

ops-monitor: If we allow canary with exception, suggest an auto-rollback policy: CPU spike or error-rate >1% for 10m -> rollback. Also enable extra tracing and perf alarms for the canary slice.

maria: Legal ok with timeboxed exception if cosign evidence is provided within 1 hour and security ok's the medium vuln as tolerable during canary. Need a line in release notes: "Security: medium-severity transitive vuln noted — patch pending." Can security produce a mitigation note?

josh: I can re-push signed attestation now. If someone triggers `deploy-bot unquarantine --evidence url` I can then re-run staging canary.

carmen: Proposal: josh re-push + attach cosign attestation, ops enable extra monitoring, QA keep canary limited to 5% traffic, legal require release-note line. If attestation doesn't appear within 60m, abort and rollback. Anyone object?

maria: approve (legal)

qa-lead: approve (QA) — will watch health dashboard

deploy-bot: Action pending: `unquarantine` requires an approver. Use `/deploybot approve-unquarantine carmen` to proceed.

carmen: /deploybot approve-unquarantine carmen

deploy-bot: [automated] Unquarantine requested by carmen. Waiting for external evidence URL.

josh: evidence uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/cosign/attest/54821

deploy-bot: Evidence verified. Unquarantine complete. Canary resumed for rc-2026-03-21 (5% traffic). Auto-rollback policy: error_rate>1% for 10m or latency >2x baseline.

ops-monitor: Monitoring on, added trace tags `canary_rc=rc-2026-03-21` and dashboards pinned. If rollback triggers, we will follow runbook "canary-auto-rollback-v2".

carmen: I'll also update release notes draft with the vuln note and a reminder to patch in next minor. Thanks all.

maria: Legal: please push the release-note text to GH: `docs/release-notes/rc-2026-03-21.md` and tag for review.

josh: done. link: https://github.com/redwood/release-notes/pull/276

qa-lead: watching — no anomalies first 15m.

carmen: keeping this thread pinned. last check in 45m to confirm stable or rollback.

ops-monitor: 15m check: healthy. continuing.

carmen: 60m mark — attestation present, canary healthy. Moving to slow rollout per plan. Closing thread after cutover.

deploy-bot: [automated] Canary -> slow-rollout initiated.
